chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Nakha'i, Abu al-Husayn, who said: Hanan ibn Sadir narrated to us, who said:
I visited [him] and forgot the two rak'ahs of the Tawaf, so I came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was at Qarn al-Tha'alib. I asked him, and he said, 'Pray in your place.'

So it is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because this report is understood to apply to one who departed from Mecca and found it difficult to return to it, so it is permissible for him at that time to pray where he remembered [the two rak'ahs], and that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الطَّوَافِ: The two units of prayer performed after the Tawaf
key_terms.صَلِّ فِي مَكَانِكَ: Pray in your place (the ruling for missing the prayer after leaving the Mataf)
key_terms.قَرْنِ الثَّعَالِبِ: A specific location near Mecca, indicating distance from the Kaaba
key_terms.مَحْمُولٌ عَلَى: Understood to apply to / interpreted as referring to

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim pray the two rak'ahs of Tawaf if they forget them and have already left the Kaaba?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in performing the two rak'ahs of Tawaf when a pilgrim has already departed the Mataf. The ruling is contextually understood as applying to those for whom returning was burdensome (*shaqqa 'alayhi*), thereby establishing a principle of ease (*rukhas*) in ritual prayer. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach of linking legal rulings to the practical circumstances of the worshipper.
